key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, welding speed, and current affect molten pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability in distinct ways.
engineering_relevance: These trends can guide parameter selection for Invar welds used in aerospace composite molds.
method: Numerical simulation of molten pool dynamics.
High-speed photography of molten pool evolution and arc behavior.
Parameter studies: 5–6 kW laser power, 0.5–0.8 m/min welding speed, and 150–170 A current.
evidence_signal: Within the tested ranges, higher laser power increased penetration and keyhole dimensions, faster welding reduced penetration and width, and higher current widened the weld and improved arc stability.
watch_item: The abstract does not report quantitative simulation-validation errors or weld mechanical properties, limiting assessment of predictive accuracy and joint performance.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
